status.detail: Border position can lag shell-managed snap geometry.

next_action.label: Design fix
next_action.reason: Trace WinEvents during Snap Layout and update the live frame.

judgment.rationale: The clarified steps and screenshot define a reproducible event-order problem. Current Always On Top code updates borders on location-change and move-size-end WinEvents, so missed or coalesced location notifications during the shell snap interaction are a plausible target.
evidence: The reporter clarified: pin a window, drag it into a Windows 11 preset, keep holding, and observe the border at the old size/position.
Current AlwaysOnTop.cpp subscribes to EVENT_OBJECT_LOCATIONCHANGE and EVENT_SYSTEM_MOVESIZEEND and calls WindowBorder::UpdateBorderPosition.
No linked fix or duplicate is present.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on current Windows 11 and harden border updates during shell snap preview/move-size transitions.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix exists; current event subscriptions provide a focused but not yet confirmed cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep the topmost border synchronized during Snap Layout resizing
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The shell’s snap-preview/move loop can change the visible frame without delivering a usable location-change update to the border window until move-size end, leaving the overlay at stale bounds during the gesture.
plan: Trace WinEvent ordering and DWM extended-frame bounds during a Snap Layout drag.
Coalesce location updates onto the module thread and refresh from the current DWM frame whenever the tracked window geometry changes during the move loop.
Add a UI regression that checks the border surrounds the live frame before and after snap completion.
verification: Pin a resizable window and drag it through each Windows 11 snap preset while holding the drag.
Confirm the border follows intermediate and final bounds without lag or orphaning.
Run Always On Top UI tests for resize, maximize, virtual desktop, and border style changes.

confidence.rationale: The subscribed events and stale-bound symptom align, but current Windows behavior must be reproduced to identify the missing or delayed notification.

issue_context.summary: During a Windows 11 Snap Layout drag, the Always On Top border can remain at the pinned window’s old bounds until the move/resize operation finishes.
known_information: The report targets PowerToys 0.63 on Windows 11 22H2 Snap Layout presets.
The stale border is visible while the drag remains active.
The current implementation already updates on location-change and move-size-end events.
inferences: A shell-managed snap transition may coalesce or delay the event used to position the separate border window.
issue_context.analysis: Because the border is a separate window, it must follow the tracked DWM frame throughout the shell interaction. Event tracing, not more reporter prose, is the next useful step.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and all three comments through 2022-10-24T12:30:52Z.
Reviewed AlwaysOnTop.cpp and WindowBorder.cpp event subscriptions and SetWindowPos updates.
No duplicate, assignee, or implementation link appears in the timeline.

actions.label: Design fix
actions.note: Approve a focused fork-side design investigation; this action does not write upstream.

reproduce.title: Trace Always On Top border during Snap Layout
steps: Pin the window with Always On Top.
Drag it to the top edge until Snap Layout presets appear.
Hover or select a preset while continuing to hold the pointer.
Observe border bounds during preview and after releasing the window.
reproduce.expected_result: The border continuously surrounds the current visible frame and never remains at the old bounds.

title: Always On Top Window Border Looks Weird When Adapting The Window Size Using On Top Windows 22H2 Presets
